cases.note: Everything declared, provided and granted.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: Nobody signed it. The bytes may be intact and nobody has attested to who produced them.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"unsigned","message":"No publisher signature accompanied this package. The bytes may be intact and nobody has attested to who produced them.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: A signature was present and did not verify. The one state that says something went wrong rather than something is missing.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"signature_failed","message":"A release signature was present and did not verify. The bytes are not the ones the signer attested to — treat this as tampering until somebody proves otherwise.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: It verified, against a key nobody here has trusted. Nothing is wrong with the bytes; what is missing is a decision.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"signature_untrusted","message":"A release signature verified, and the key that made it is not one this robot trusts. Nothing is wrong with the bytes; what is missing is the operator's decision that this signer may publish here.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: The platform cannot check. A gap in the operating system rather than in the package, and the remedy belongs on a different desk.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"signature_unverifiable","message":"This platform cannot verify a release signature, so nothing has established who produced these bytes. That is a gap in the operating system rather than in the package.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: The contents do not hash to the manifest digest.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"digest_mismatch","message":"The package contents do not hash to the digest in its manifest.","severity":"error","subjects":["sha256:pkg","sha256:other"]}]}

cases.note: An environment describes a simulated world — simulators, a scene, assets, physics and render rates — and only a simulator RHAL driver can load one. A warning rather than an error: installing it is not dangerous, and refusing it would stop an operator staging a package onto a robot they are about to point at a simulator. What is not acceptable is silence.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[{"code":"environment_inert","message":"An environment describes a simulated world, and no simulator driver is loaded on this robot. It will install, and nothing will ever load it.","severity":"warning"}]}

cases.note: The same package where it belongs. The flag comes from the descriptor, where §35.3 puts the obligation to declare.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: §55.1: "its `required_capabilities` are still checked at admission, since an environment that needs a gripper is not runnable by a robot without one in sim either". Two findings, and the capability one is the error.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"capability_ungranted","message":"This robot does not provide capabilities the package requires.","severity":"error","subjects":["locomotion.walk"]}]}

cases.note: The flag changes nothing for any other kind. A simulator is a robot as far as admission is concerned, which is the whole point of §35.3 — the thing being tested has to be the thing that ships.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: Only drivers touch hardware directly.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"isolation_violation","message":"A policy package may not run unsandboxed. Only drivers touch hardware directly.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: A driver is the one kind that may.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: A robot that cannot feed the package refuses it before it runs.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"budget_exceeded","message":"This robot cannot supply the resources the package declares it needs.","severity":"error","subjects":["RAM: needs 512 MB, has 256 MB"]}]}

cases.note: Each shortfall is named separately.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"budget_exceeded","message":"This robot cannot supply the resources the package declares it needs.","severity":"error","subjects":["RAM: needs 512 MB, has 128 MB","VRAM: needs 2048 MB, has 512 MB","Disk: needs 4096 MB, has 100 MB","CPU: needs 2 cores, has 1"]}]}

cases.note: An undeclared capacity is zero, not unlimited.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"budget_exceeded","message":"This robot cannot supply the resources the package declares it needs.","severity":"error","subjects":["VRAM: needs 2048 MB, has 0 MB","Disk: needs 4096 MB, has 0 MB","CPU: needs 2 cores, has 0"]}]}

cases.note: A package cannot request what it never declared a need for.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"over_request","message":"The package requests permissions it never declared a need for.","severity":"error","subjects":["locomotion.walk"]}]}

cases.note: The card fields declare what the package needs and the embodiment block is empty, so nothing enforced them. The worst shape this can take: a green install of an unchecked package.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"embodiment_undeclared","message":"This package declares requirements its embodiment block does not, so admission checked nothing for them. §8.2 enforces `embodiment.capabilities` and `embodiment.extensions`.","severity":"error","subjects":["manipulation.grasp","unitree.raw_lowlevel"]}]}

cases.note: The two spellings carry the same tokens, which is the shape a publisher who filled in both should get, and it is not a finding.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: Declaring more in `embodiment` than on the card is a Hub that under-reports what the package needs, not a robot that under-enforces them. The subset test runs one way for that reason: refusing here would refuse the package whose enforced declaration is the stricter one.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: The operator profile withholds it outright.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"capability_denied","message":"The operator profile withholds capabilities this package requires.","severity":"error","subjects":["manipulation.grasp"]}]}

cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"capability_ungranted","message":"This robot does not provide capabilities the package requires.","severity":"error","subjects":["manipulation.grasp"]}]}

cases.note: A malformed version both editions have always agreed about, and the one that decided the §80 question. `Number("")` is 0 and a failed Rust parse fell back to 0, so "1..0" is exactly "1.0.0" and the package installs. It is pinned unchanged across the 2026-09-05 rule change, because a segment with no leading digits is still 0 — which is the argument that settled the neighbouring cases below: the reference was already treating one unreadable segment as zero, so treating the rest as NaN was not a rule, it was an inconsistency.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: The §80 open question, decided 2026-09-05 and pinned here. A robot on "1.2.0-rc1" asked for a package needing "1.2.1". Until this rule the reference read "0-rc1" as NaN, reported the robot as *newer* than the minimum and **admitted** it — so any robot whose version had one non-numeric segment satisfied every `min_os_version` there has ever been. It is refused, and the refusal is the point of the field.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"os_too_old","message":"Requires Skynet OS 1.2.1 or later; this robot runs 1.2.0-rc1.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: The other half of the same decision, and the reason the rule is *leading digits* rather than the whole segment falling back to 0. A robot on "1.2.10-rc1" needs "1.2.5". Reading the segment as 0 would refuse it and say "Requires Skynet OS 1.2.5 or later; this robot runs 1.2.10-rc1" — a sentence naming a version that looks newer than the one demanded, which §64 makes a defect rather than a cosmetic problem. It installs: a candidate compares as the release it is a candidate for.
cases.expected: {"admitted":true,"effective_grants":["manipulation.grasp"],"findings":[]}

cases.note: No leading digit, so the segment is 0 and the robot is the oldest version there is. Fail closed, which is the property the whole rule is chosen for.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"os_too_old","message":"Requires Skynet OS 1.2.1 or later; this robot runs 1.2.rc1.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: The hole, pinned shut. `Number("Infinity")` is infinity and the Rust `"Infinity".parse::<f64>()` is infinity too, so this was the rare malformed version the two editions *agreed* on — and agreed to admit, against every minimum simultaneously. There is no leading digit, so it is 0.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"os_too_old","message":"Requires Skynet OS 2.0.0 or later; this robot runs Infinity.0.0.","severity":"error"}]}

cases.note: The warning channel requested *and* withheld by the operator profile. §49.1 is checked before the denials on purpose — a reserved token is not something an operator declined, it is something nobody can grant — so `capability_reserved` is reported first and the operator is told the one they can never give. No other case has a token that is both.
cases.expected: {"admitted":false,"effective_grants":[],"findings":[{"code":"capability_reserved","message":"The audible warning before autonomous motion is a system function and no grant confers it. A package that could claim this channel could silence its own warning, which removes a control the operator's risk assessment relied on (§49.1).","severity":"error","subjects":["hri.warning"]},{"code":"capability_denied","message":"The operator profile withholds capabilities this package requires.","severity":"error","subjects":["hri.warning"]}]}
